title: Informal Conjecture on Universal N0 for Bumping a Ladder
statement_text: There exists a constant $N_0$ such that for every $k\ge1$, every $3$-connected graph containing a union of $N_0$ vertex-disjoint copies of the ladder $L_k$ as a minor contains $L_{k+1}$ as a minor. For all we know, this might even be true with $N_0 = 4$.
context_text: $L_k$ denotes the ladder with $k$ rungs, i.e. the $2\times k$ grid graph. The authors prove the 'bumping a ladder' theorem: for every integer $k\ge1$ there is an integer $N$ such that every $3$-connected graph containing a union of $N$ vertex-disjoint copies of $L_k$ as a minor contains $L_{k+1}$ as a minor. This generalizes the fact that a connected graph with two vertex-disjoint paths of order $k$ has a path of order $k+1$; combined with a theorem of Robertson and Seymour on packing disjoint copies of a planar minor, it gives that every $3$-connected graph without an $L_{k+1}$ minor has a set of boundedly many vertices whose removal destroys all $L_k$ minors. The $3$-connectivity is necessary: there is a $2$-connected graph with $8$ disjoint copies of $L_4$ and no $L_5$ minor. In their proof $N$ depends on $k$, but the authors expect this dependence is not necessary and conjecture a universal constant.

title: Open Problem: Characterization of Unavoidable Graphs
statement_text: Obtain a full characterization of unavoidable graphs, where a graph $H$ is unavoidable if the cover graph of every poset with large enough dimension contains $H$ as a minor.
context_text: For a poset $P$, $y$ covers $x$ if $x<y$ and no $z$ satisfies $x<z<y$; the cover graph of $P$ is the graph on its ground set where two elements are adjacent if one covers the other (the Hasse diagram as an undirected graph). The dimension of $P$ is the least number of linear orders whose intersection is the order of $P$. A graph $H$ is unavoidable if the cover graph of every poset of large enough dimension contains $H$ as a minor; the class of unavoidable graphs is minor-closed. Kelly's classical construction gives posets of unbounded dimension whose cover graphs are planar and have pathwidth $3$, so every unavoidable graph is a minor of a graph from Kelly's construction (equivalently, of a graph obtained by gluing copies of $K_4$ along edges in a path-like way and subdividing once all their 'horizontal' edges, as depicted in the paper). The authors prove that posets whose cover graphs exclude a fixed ladder ($2\times k$ grid) as a minor have bounded dimension, so all ladders (and hence their minors, e.g. fans) are unavoidable; besides ladders, the only other known positive result is that $K_4$ is unavoidable. They conjecture that the necessary condition given by Kelly's construction is also sufficient.
notes: Stated in prose as 'it is an open problem'; no labelled environment. Conjecture 6 in the same paper proposes a conjectured answer.

title: Conjecture 6
statement_text: A graph $H$ is unavoidable if and only if $H$ is a minor of some graph from Kelly's construction.
context_text: For a poset $P$, $y$ covers $x$ if $x<y$ and no $z$ satisfies $x<z<y$; the cover graph of $P$ is the graph on its ground set where two elements are adjacent if one covers the other (the Hasse diagram as an undirected graph). The authors prove that posets whose cover graphs exclude a fixed ladder ($2\times k$ grid) as a minor have bounded dimension, so every ladder is unavoidable; the only other known positive result is that $K_4$ is unavoidable. The conjecture asserts that the necessary condition from Kelly's construction is also sufficient, which would give a full characterization of unavoidable graphs.
